novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 / related_work / project_justification
novelty_flags.one_line: The comparison incorrectly claims a new full-adjacency or observed-surrogate recovery regime: Prashant et al.'s Theorem 3 identifies the binary adjacency matrix up to latent permutation, and its Theorem 2 explicitly relates higher-layer latent ranks to measured pure descendants; retain the quadratic-query compression as the actual delta.

soundness_flags.label: def:observed-rank-oracle; estimand_functional; Theorem 1
soundness_flags.one_line: R is not yet a functional of P_X: conditional means and conditional latent laws are defined only P_XA-a.e., while their C1 extensions and pointwise derivatives can differ on thin supports, changing the essential-supremum Jacobian rank.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 3
soundness_flags.one_line: Given def:replay-certificate, acceptance is defined as successful deterministic replay of RankPeel, so both acceptance and its converse follow from the definitions plus Theorems 1–2 rather than a substantive certificate theorem.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3 identifies the binary adjacency matrix M up to latent permutations from the rank function, and the text says the recursion identifies the entire graph structure; Theorem 2 uses measured pure descendants as surrogates. Appendix A.7 performs exhaustive subset checks for pure blocks and parent subsets.

The paper defines covariance-rank faithfulness, identifies the minimum latent d-separator through covariance rank in its linear IL2H model, and uses measured pure descendants as surrogates before an algorithm targeting a Markov equivalence class.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–2, Introduction and Definitions 2.1–2.4; p. 5, Theorem 3.5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper identifies nonlinear latent hierarchical structures and latent variables up to invertible maps under a distinct representation-recovery assumption set, and gives an explicit estimation procedure.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Statistics 38(3), publisher version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives trek-separation rank characterizations for Gaussian graphical models using covariance matrices and trek-rule determinant arguments; it does not state a nonlinear conditional-mean-Jacobian result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make R version-invariant before retaining the unchanged-class claim: impose a support/version condition sufficient to identify the C1 conditional-mean jet P_XA-a.e., or replace R by an explicitly observed-law-invariant weak/local derivative functional and reprove the restricted separator lemma for it.

Rewrite the Prashant comparison to acknowledge published full adjacency and measured-pure-descendant recursion; isolate the strict result as a proven quadratic versus exhaustive query-complexity separation, ideally with a lower bound or an explicit count for the published procedure.
Demote replay certification to a corollary or replace it with a non-definitional, sound obstruction/incompatibility certificate for rank transcripts that can reject every graph in the model class.

recommended_next_step: Revise the oracle’s observed-law definition and the Prashant comparison, then retain RankPeel only as the explicit quadratic-query construction rather than as a new full-adjacency or observed-surrogate identification regime.
